notes: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the current month's closing savings, plus a fix to the redeem picker. THE PROBLEM, MEASURED: the Projection sheet and the Dashboard/Net Worth pages ran SEPARATE implementations of the same concept — _eomSavingsChain and projectSavingsChain — and had drifted Rs 92,144 apart on identical data. Every correction from this round (one-time budgets applied per item, the close built from live savings plus the salary account, balance adjustments surviving into the close, per-instrument remaining contributions, the redemption double-count) lived only in the Projection sheet. A logged adjustment showed correctly on one page and was silently dropped on the others. This divergence had been flagged twice before and deferred; it grew rather than went away, which is what happens when two implementations of one idea are maintained side by side. THE FIX: a single shared function, sharedCurrentMonthClose(p), now computes the current month for BOTH callers. Measured first before scoping — the gap was constant across all months and grew only by interest, proving it originated entirely in the current month and then rode forward, so aligning that one month aligns the entire chain. Verified: five consecutive months now agree to Rs 0, from a starting gap of Rs 92,144. Past months still reverse-walk from logged transactions and future months still chain as previous close plus planned residue, in both places. A fallback to the previous arithmetic is retained should the shared function be unavailable. SCENARIO-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: the shared function starts from the engine's planned expense for the month, which already carries scenario effects, and adds only the OVERSPEND per line. Since counted = max(actual, budget) = budget + max(0, actual - budget), summing over lines gives engine_planned + total_overspend, and a line with no budget at all (unplanned one-time spending) contributes its full amount. Checked against a worked month: Rs 2,86,557 planned + Rs 8,537 unplanned = Rs 2,95,094, matching the sheet exactly. REDEEM PICKER: now shows what the Projection page's Running Balances row shows. The previous version additionally subtracted every redemption ever logged, which drove any instrument with redemption history to zero — Mutual Funds displayed Rs 0 despite holding Rs 3.95 L, because Rs 4.3 L of historic redemptions were deducted from a balance that already reflected them. Verified against the sheet: picker Rs 3.95 L vs Running Balances Rs 3,94,999, and FD Rs 5.50 L against Rs 5,50,000. NOTE ON THE LIQUIDITY TILES: _liveLiquidCash is deliberately left alone. It answers 'cash right now', not 'cash at month end', so it is legitimately a different number and not part of this divergence. STILL TO VERIFY ON YOUR SIDE: this touches the chain that Net Worth, the over-time chart, the composition bar and the retirement projection all read from. Re-run SELF_TEST.js and PROPAGATION_TEST_{1,2,3}.js. Expect the headline net worth to DROP by roughly the size of the old gap — that is the correction, not a new fault.
